slides.lead: Its official name is a Temporary Use Ban, or TUB.
Only water companies can bring in a TUB, under section 76 of the Water Industry Act 1991. First they must tell customers, and publish it on their website and in two local newspapers.

steps: Water your garden or plants at home.
Clean a private car or leisure boat.
Fill or maintain a paddling or swimming pool.
Fill a domestic pond or ornamental fountain.
Draw water for recreation at home.

paras: Water plants with a watering can, or with rain from a water butt.
Wash your car with a bucket, and reuse household water on plants.

slides.lead: In past droughts, TUBs cut the water put into supply by 3 to 5%.
And 76% said bans are effective, in Environment Agency research.

paras: Thames Water, Southern Water, South East Water and Yorkshire Water all had bans in part or all of their areas.

tips: More water stays in rivers for wildlife.
Reservoirs last longer into a dry spell.
Everyone sees that water is scarce.
